questions.q: What is 'drift' in the context of Terraform?
options: A bug in the Terraform CLI itself
When real infrastructure no longer matches what Terraform's configuration and state say it should be
The time delay between plan and apply
A type of provider plugin
questions.explain: Drift happens when infrastructure is changed outside of Terraform — for example manually in a console — so it no longer matches the configuration.

questions.q: Does running terraform plan on its own change any real infrastructure?
options: No, but it deletes the state file
No, it only compares configuration and state against reality and reports differences
Yes, but only in the default workspace
Yes, it always applies minor changes automatically
questions.explain: terraform plan is read-only with respect to infrastructure — it reports what would change without actually making any changes.

questions.q: What does the -detailed-exitcode flag add to a scheduled terraform plan check?
options: It automatically applies any drift found
It disables state locking
It makes the plan run faster
It exits with code 2 instead of 0 when there are pending changes, so a CI job can detect and alert on drift
questions.explain: -detailed-exitcode distinguishes 'no changes' (exit 0) from 'changes pending' (exit 2), which lets a CI pipeline fail and notify someone when drift is detected.

questions.q: In the lesson's example drift plan output, what does the line showing size change from one value to another indicate?
options: The provider version is outdated
The resource is about to be destroyed
The real VM's size no longer matches what the Terraform configuration says it should be
A new resource is about to be created
questions.explain: The '~' update symbol with an old and new size value shows Terraform detected the actual VM size differs from what the configuration specifies — a sign of drift.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what are the two honest ways to resolve detected drift?
options: Ignore it until the next scheduled apply, or delete the resource
Switch to a different Terraform workspace
Always re-apply immediately without reviewing what changed
Update the configuration to match a legitimate manual change, or re-apply to correct an unwanted one
questions.explain: Drift should either be accepted and reflected in updated configuration (reviewed like any other change), or corrected by re-applying the existing configuration — never left unresolved.
